guide.title: Quick Guide
guide.subtitle: Get started with PC Workman
guide.step1_body:
This tool monitors and optimizes your PC in real time.
Use the sidebar to navigate between sections.
guide.step2_body:
Go to MONITORING & ALERTS to watch
temperature, voltage and system health live.
guide.step3_body:
Head to Optimization → Startup to manage
programs that launch with Windows.
guide.step4_body:
Use the AI assistant on the right panel
to ask questions about your hardware.
guide.finale_body: You can expand any section or close the guide.

ram_flush.title: Auto RAM Flush
ram_flush.desc: Free working-set memory when usage is high
ram_flush.info:
Forces Windows to trim the working set of all running processes,
releasing unused physical memory back to the system pool.
Triggers automatically when RAM stays above threshold for 30 s.

turbo_pp.title: Turbo Power Plan
turbo_pp.desc: Auto-switch to custom 'Turbo PC' plan on demand
turbo_pp.info:
Creates a custom 'Turbo PC' plan based on High Performance.
CPU stays at max frequency - no throttling.
App exit auto-restores your original plan.
Requires Administrator rights.

app_hibernation.title: App Hibernation
app_hibernation.desc: Sleep apps unused for X minutes

upgrade_advisor.title: Upgrade Advisor
upgrade_advisor.desc: What to upgrade, read from your own load history
upgrade_advisor.no_data: Not enough history yet - let PC Workman run a day or two in the background, then reopen.
upgrade_advisor.v_ram: RAM is the pressure point - adding memory is the cheapest, surest win.
upgrade_advisor.v_cpu: CPU is the bottleneck - it runs near its limit while the GPU has spare power.
upgrade_advisor.v_gpu: GPU is the bottleneck - it runs flat out while the CPU has headroom.
upgrade_advisor.v_ok: No screaming bottleneck - upgrade only when a specific app or game feels slow.

cpu_throttle.title: CPU Throttle Guard
cpu_throttle.desc: Is it thermal, power or headroom? Live verdict in OVERCLOCK
cpu_throttle.info: Instead of 'preventing throttling' automatically, PC Workman DIAGNOSES first: are the clocks held by temperature, the power budget (TDP/PL2), or is there headroom? Live verdict in the OVERCLOCK Headroom Lab. Read-only, zero risk.

browser_cache.title: Browser Cache Cleaner
browser_cache.desc: Large files, duplicates, old installers - preview before delete
browser_cache.info: Safe Storage Advisor: finds large files, duplicates, old installers and Downloads clutter. Deletes NOTHING without a full preview. Browser cache is not automatically treated as junk.

bg_limiter.title: Background Limiter
bg_limiter.desc: Gently deprioritize background hogs under pressure, auto-restore
bg_limiter.info: Responsiveness Guard: under real CPU pressure it temporarily lowers background process priority (Efficiency Mode), never touches the OS, anti-cheats or your active app. State restores automatically and every decision is logged.

net_reset.title: Network Adapter Reset
net_reset.desc: Reset adapter stack on connectivity issues
net_reset.info:
Runs netsh winsock reset and flushes DNS to resolve
stale network states without a full reboot.

reg_clean.title: Registry Junk Cleaner
reg_clean.desc: Find leftovers of an uninstalled app - preview, never blind-delete
reg_clean.info: App Leftover Scanner: traces ONE uninstalled application (startup entries, services, tasks, folders, clearly linked registry keys) and previews everything before any removal. Blind registry cleaning was removed on purpose - Microsoft discourages it.

gpu_watchdog.title: GPU Driver Watchdog
gpu_watchdog.desc: Detect and restart hung GPU driver
gpu_watchdog.info:
Polls GPU state via nvidia-smi / WMI and triggers
a TDR reset if the driver stops responding.

log_rotate.title: Log File Rotation
log_rotate.desc: Correlate slowdowns with new startup apps, services and drivers
log_rotate.info: What Changed?: when the PC slows down, PC Workman correlates it with changes - a new startup app, service, driver or Windows update. Learned history instead of guessing.

dns_nightly.title: DNS Auto-Flush
dns_nightly.desc: Nightly DNS cache flush on schedule
dns_nightly.info:
Schedules a silent DNS flush every night at 03:00
to prevent stale cache entries from breaking browsing.

fw_monitor.title: Firewall Health
fw_monitor.desc: Verify Windows Firewall is active and healthy
fw_monitor.info:
Queries netsh advfirewall state and alerts if any
profile (Domain / Private / Public) is disabled.

receipts.desc: Before/after proof for every action - no snake oil
receipts.head: Every action gets a receipt: BEFORE at trigger, AFTER ~20 s later.
receipts.empty: No receipts yet - run FLUSH RAM and the first one appears here.

fan_control.no_sensor_body: Windows does not report fan speed to applications. PC Workman reads it from LibreHardwareMonitor when that program is running with its web server turned on (Options > Remote Web Server > Run).
fan_control.no_sensor_note: Until then this page stays empty. PC Workman never shows estimated or example fan speeds.
fan_control.source_line: Read from {source}, refreshed every few seconds.
fan_control.hist_empty_body: The chart draws measured fan speed only. It starts filling as soon as a fan sensor is available and PC Workman keeps running.
fan_control.hist_collecting: Collecting the first samples. The line appears after about ten seconds.
fan_control.hist_since_start: History is kept while PC Workman is running (up to 12 hours).
fan_control.plan_note: Planner: curves are saved in PC Workman. They do not change fan speed yet; your fans follow the BIOS or the vendor tool.
fan_control.apply_saved:
Saved. This curve is now your fan plan and reloads when you open this page.

PC Workman does not control fan speed yet. Your fans keep following the BIOS or the vendor tool.

monitoring.desc: Watches temperatures, load and voltages, learns this machine's normal, and flags what breaks the pattern.

learn.info: ℹ The longer it runs, the better it knows YOUR normal - and the smarter the temperature & voltage alerts become.
learn.learning_for: ⏱ Learning for {since}  ·  {hrs}h of your machine observed
learn.unlock_cpu: ↳ CPU temp: run LibreHardwareMonitor to unlock
learn.explain_new: Every 5 minutes PC Workman notes the temperature and load for what you are doing: idle, light work, gaming. After about {h} hours of normal use it knows what is usual here and alerts only when something is not. Leave it running.
learn.explain_learning: The usual workloads are learned. The rest fill in as you use the PC that way; nothing to do on purpose.
learn.explain_done: Alerts compare every reading with what is normal for this PC under the same kind of load.
learn.time_travel_sub: the full history behind what was learned
learn.rare: Rare on this PC, learned along the way: {list}
